intro: Registrations show which cars moved. Finance & insurance (F&I) and value-add products show how the deal was paid for and what it earned, and in Australia that half of the business has been rebuilt by regulation since 2018. Below are the metrics I'd track, how the lender channels compare, and the hypotheses I'd test as the market goes electric.
guardrail: Public information and frameworks only. No employer, dealership, lender or customer figures appear on this page.

metrics.name: Finance penetration
metrics.why: The headline F&I health number. Split it by drivetrain and by brand before reading anything into it.

metrics.name: Products per retail unit
metrics.why: Shows whether protection products (tyre & rim, paint, GAP) are being offered and accepted consistently, separately from finance.

metrics.name: F&I income per retail unit
metrics.why: The number that tells you whether the back end is carrying the front end, which matters more as new-car margins compress.

metrics.name: Look-to-book
metrics.why: Separates a lender-appetite problem from a desk-process problem. Read it per lender, not just in total.

metrics.name: Contracts in transit
metrics.formula: days from delivery to lender funding
metrics.why: A cash-flow metric. Slow funding ties up working capital even when the front-end numbers look healthy.

lenders.title: Lender channels compared
lenders.subtitle: Typical patterns only. They vary by lender, campaign and customer profile.
rows: Subsidised campaign rates; approvals aligned to the brand's model launches
Volume can swing with campaign calendars; rate support is a marketing cost, not a given
Rate support and guaranteed-future-value style products are a lever for moving new EV models
Price for strong-credit customers; existing banking relationships
Customers often arrive pre-approved, so the finance happens outside the dealership
Several banks advertise discounted "green" car-loan rates for low-emission vehicles
Approval breadth and speed: self-employed borrowers, thin credit files
Higher rates; affordability and responsible-lending checks deserve extra care
Uncertain used-EV residual values can show up in pricing and balloon settings
Tax: eligible EVs are exempt from fringe benefits tax under salary packaging
Usually arranged through the employer's provider, not the dealership's F&I desk
Probably the biggest single reason dealer finance penetration on EVs can look low

hypotheses.title: Novated leasing pulls EV finance out of the showroom
hypotheses.body: Expect lower dealer finance penetration on battery-electric than on combustion models of the same brand.
hypotheses.test: Split penetration by drivetrain, and flag deliveries known to be novated.

hypotheses.title: Long battery warranties shrink the extended-warranty pitch
hypotheses.body: With manufacturer battery cover commonly around eight years, product mix should shift towards protection products and GAP.
hypotheses.test: Compare products per retail unit and product mix by drivetrain, period on period.

hypotheses.title: Used-EV price softness makes GAP and balloon sizing matter more
hypotheses.body: Faster depreciation raises negative-equity risk. Since 2021, though, most add-on insurance can't be sold on delivery day.
hypotheses.test: Track conversion of deferred-sale offers, not just same-day attachment.

hypotheses.title: Compressed new-car gross shifts profit to the back end
hypotheses.body: As price competition from new entrants squeezes front-end margin, F&I and value-add become a larger share of gross per unit.
hypotheses.test: Track F&I income as a share of total gross per unit, by brand, over time.

timeline.what: ASIC Report 492 on add-on insurance sold through car dealers
timeline.why: Found the market was failing consumers and set up the reforms that followed.

timeline.what: ASIC ban on flex commissions in car finance
timeline.why: Dealers can no longer earn more by setting a higher interest rate. Income per contract now depends on volume and product mix.
Recommended a deferred sales model for add-on insurance.

timeline.what: Deferred sales model for add-on insurance; design and distribution obligations
timeline.why: A four-day pause between the car sale and most add-on insurance sales, plus target-market rules for financial products.

timeline.what: Electric Car Discount: FBT exemption for eligible EVs
timeline.why: Made novated leasing the cheapest way for many employees to finance an EV.

timeline.what: Plug-in hybrids drop out of the FBT exemption
timeline.why: Except under existing commitments, which tilts novated demand towards pure battery-electric.
